stage1.impression: A tidy CG showroom: a fir-lined niche with two identical black monitors on lit plinths, a big empty brown floor, a near-white artwork at left and chair backs cut by the bottom edge. At 1:1 the fir is denoiser-smeared into streaks, the spots blow out the boards above each speaker, the speakers read as generic dark studio monitors, not tinted acrylic, and nothing says anyone has been here. As it stands no magazine would run it as a specific place; it reads as a generic home-cinema or hi-fi showroom render.

blocking_9: The speakers must read at a glance as tinted smoked acrylic with light through them (speaker region lum_median >= 45, the white batts visible through the cabinet) rather than black boxes
No clipped fir above the speakers: clip_pct < 0.5 % for the frame and under 2 % in the niche's top band [200,100,630,170]
Clean full-resolution render: no denoiser smear on the fir grain, the felt or the speaker edges (more samples, final scale 1.0)
Signs of life and the zone's own furniture in frame: an Orb on a hex oak table, a glass, a record, so the room reads as the listening bar and not as a showroom
The floor (a fifth of the frame) needs a pool of light and texture rather than an even featureless brown plane
The artwork/screen at left must not be the brightest large surface in the frame (median 182 against a speaker at 31)

defects.what: Altar spot hotspot on the fir above the right speaker, 45 % clipped, blown white
Same hotspot above the left speaker, 48 % clipped
Right speaker reads as an opaque black monitor: median 30.8, the smoked tint and the batts behind it are lost; the horn reads as a dark plastic box
Left speaker likewise dark (median 31.4); with the right one it is an identical copy at the same angle, which reads as a duplicated model
Denoiser smear: the fir boards' grain turns into vertical watercolour streaks, the felt panels are flat untextured rectangles
The screen at left is near white (median 182) and flat, pulling the eye away from the altar and reading as a projector screen
Carpet is an even featureless plane (lum_range 29) with no pile, no pool of light and no furniture, a large dead area
Ceiling beams 27 % crushed, the fir beams' checks and grain lost
Tub chair and a head cut awkwardly by the frame edge at bottom left
Chair backs cut by the bottom edge, unreadable as velvet tub chairs
Plinth glow line reads as a thin LED strip / display plinth

changes.problem: The altar spots blow out the fir above each speaker while leaving the speakers themselves dark, so the hero is the darkest object in its niche.

change.from: 140.0 W, cone 44 deg, aimed down the boards
change.to: 70 W, cone 30 deg, re-aimed onto the speakers' faces from about 1.5 m forward of the niche, so the beam lands on the cabinet and horn, not on the boards above

changes.expected: No white bloom on the fir; the cabinets catch a soft warm key; speaker median rises toward 45-60

changes.problem: The smoked acrylic reads as opaque black because nothing lights it from within or behind, so the tint and batts never show.

change.setting: on each speaker 4 x area (the speaker lamps)
change.to: 0.6 W/m2 at the target, 2900 K, placed behind and beside the cabinet so light passes through the acrylic and rims its polished edges

changes.expected: The cabinet glows smoky amber at its edges, the white batts read through it, the horn's resin catches a rim

changes.problem: Denoiser smear erases the fir grain and the felt texture, the clearest CG tell in the frame.

evidence.measured: 3x crop shows vertical watercolour streaks in place of grain; felt panels flat

change.to: 1024 samples, adaptive 0.005, final at scale 1.0 (2400 x 1600), denoiser with albedo+normal passes, then a 0.3 % film grain in post

changes.expected: Board grain, nail holes and the felt's weave survive at 1:1; edges of the acrylic stay crisp

changes.problem: The screen at left is the largest bright surface in the frame and competes with the altar.

change.setting: the room's glowing surfaces: the screens' images

changes.expected: The screen sits as a dim grey image in the dark wall, well below the speakers

changes.problem: The camera stands back with a wide lens, so a fifth of the frame is empty carpet and the tub chairs are cut at the edge; the zone's own furniture (hex tables, Orbs) is out of shot.

evidence.measured: carpet lum_range 29, nothing on it; chairs cropped at [0,330,80,480] and [430,430,640,480]

change.to: seated eye level about 1.15 m, from behind and beside one tub chair at about [13.6, 2.2, 1.15], 35 mm, so a chair's velvet shoulder and a hex oak table with a lit Orb sit in the near foreground and the pair fills the upper middle third

changes.expected: Foreground depth (chair, table, Orb pool of light), the altar larger in frame, no dead floor

changes.problem: No sign of life in the zone: the props listed all sit at the bar, out of shot.

evidence.measured: no glass, record, coat or sleeve visible anywhere

change.from: rocks glasses, coupe, record, coat at the counter
change.to: add in the zone: a half-drunk rocks glass and a record sleeve on the nearest hex table, a coat over a tub chair's arm, a record leaning on the altar plinth

changes.expected: The frame reads as a used room at night, not a showroom

changes.problem: The floor has no pool of light, so the space between the seats and the altar is dead and flat.

change.setting: the Orbs (and the Domes' downlights if any fall in the zone)
change.to: each Orb 4 W, glow 0.25, so each hex table throws a warm pool onto the carpet; carpet material roughness up with a pile/bump texture

changes.expected: Pools of light with dark between them on the floor; carpet reads as pile

changes.problem: The fir beams overhead are crushed to black, so the shell's main material is lost.

change.setting: haze and a ceiling uplight bounce
change.to: haze 0.005, plus a dim warm grazing wash (about 20 W, 2400 K) up the beams from the niche's top edge

changes.expected: Beams hold checks and grain in the shadows; a little atmosphere in the spot beams

out_of_scope.request: Make the two altar speakers differ in pose or toe-in so they do not read as a duplicated model
out_of_scope.why: The pair's placement and toe-in are fixed by the room's design; a camera off the axis of symmetry (c5) reduces the effect instead

out_of_scope.request: Replace the thin glowing strip on the plinths with a softer, wider light plinth
out_of_scope.why: The light plinth is part of the altar's design as the card fixes it; only its brightness could change

out_of_scope.request: Make the smoked tint more saturated so the speaker carries the frame's colour
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's colour is fixed; only the light through it can be changed (c2)
